### Alignment A2: jvmcontract align proposes method correspondence between two builds, ranked, written to the hints file

change `prrxuoknonuz` · [log `ecff2f691d4e`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/11f93b59-b830-4090-8775-33313957ef5c/ecff2f691d4e1d28381dddef4dadce90759417f1bc56b30657f95c4157ddfbfa.jsonl.gz)

A new module, lib/src/alignment.rs, and the command jvmcontract align --before DIR --after DIR [--hints FILE] [--json]. It works statically and proves nothing. An old method the new build declares with the same class, name and descriptor corresponds to itself and to nothing else. For a vanished one, the candidates are the new build's new methods tied to it by the same name (in its class or moved), the same body shape, a similar body, a caller in common, or the same parameters in the same class. Each tie adds weight to a score. The first candidate leads only with at least 3 points and 3 ahead of the next; otherwise the choice is a person's. --hints replaces the file's inferred proposals and keeps every hint a person stated or approved. Hint gains two optional fields, rank and why (the shared IR, added only; the golden files are unchanged).

Scored on the A1 ground truth with the new examples/tools/alignment.py score, recorded in examples/tools/alignment/scores/A2-methods.json and on its page. Methods that kept their name: 15 of 15 found. Moved: 2 of 2 found. Renamed: 1 found, 1 asked (122, whose only tie is its parameters). Nothing was wrong or missed. Caveat: the same-parameters tie and the lead threshold were set after a first run, and the table and the scorer come from this stream, so the score shows agreement with the table, not generality. Verified with 2 unit tests and 7 tests in lib/tests/alignment.rs on javac-compiled pairs and the joint example's kernel, and 15 Python tests in test_alignment.py; the foundations integration test still passes (alignment still unsupported there until A4's field correspondence). lib/README.md documents the command.

### Alignment A3 (static half): align maps each matched pair's arguments, records and result under the preservation contract, scored on examples 121-139

change `vvtltnmzuwru` · [log `39ba85dbce2b`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/11f93b59-b830-4090-8775-33313957ef5c/39ba85dbce2b8161e4587d36779118ccb78dfc7755bb7571986630b794cafead.jsonl.gz)

jvmcontract align now relates, for every method pair it matches, how each old input is made from the new inputs and how the results compare, in the form --before-arguments and --results-agree-when take (lib/src/alignment/mappings.rs). It works under the comparison's preservation contract (the new --contract option, or for a standalone method the one its two signatures imply): an input the contract fixes is mapped to itself and nothing else, a stated derivation is used as stated, and candidates are only names, field paths, an integral cast and records built with their constructors, never arithmetic, so the offset mapping before.c = after.c + 1 cannot be proposed. Internal inputs (a parameter gathered into a record, a record that gained a component) are ranked by name, type and position, a weak or tied match is a question, and new inputs nothing uses are left free. Results come from a small catalogue (equal, widened, wrapped or unwrapped, compared on the old components, or a changed meaning put to a person as a question), and every required observation stays in the accounting. Proposals go to the hints file as inferred, proposed, unchecked correspondences.

Verified with 8 new tests in lib/tests/alignment.rs (the planted offset case with and without a contract among them), 4 in examples/tools/test_alignment.py, and the whole cargo suite; the integration contract still reports alignment as unsupported, now naming A4. Scored on the A1 table (examples/tools/alignment/scores/A3-mappings.json): 50 of 50 anchored inputs, 8 of 8 internal, 4 of 4 new inputs left free, 17 of 17 inferred results found, and the 2 changed results (122, 123) asked; nothing wrong or missed, and the proposals amount to the examples' own hand-written flags. The rules were written with that table in view, so this shows consistency, not generality. No proofs yet: checking proposals by the regression proof is A3's second half, after A4's narrow case.

### Alignment A3 (second half): align --prove checks every proposal by the regression proof, collapses by proof, and settles each pair (verification pending)

change `wrwkmlpxuzoy` · [log `4d7819cc24cb`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/11f93b59-b830-4090-8775-33313957ef5c/4d7819cc24cb4806409952fa20c4182fff17183a4b6903b77fff2ca98e5f3296.jsonl.gz)

jvmcontract align --prove (lib/src/alignment/proofs.rs) runs the regression check (equivalence::run, as a caller) on every complete mapping align proposes for a pair, with the flags it amounts to, under the scope and proof options given. A vacuous proof counts as none. Proved mappings with the same result relation are collapsed into one candidate: each makes the old version's observations a function of the new one's on every input of the claim, so nothing a consumer sees tells them apart. Each pair is then settled: one proved (evidence 'proved for claim key K', intent still proposed; for a standalone method, the relation is proved and whether it is the intended one is unconfirmed; for a changed result, approving it is a person's decision), several relations proved (a question), or none (each mapping tried, with its counterexample). The hints file carries each proposal's evidence. The claim key is provisional (a digest of the tool, both builds' class files, the flags and settings) until the summaries stream's canonical key exists. Field-equation proposals are not tried: they have no flag form, and their proof is the heap stream's.

The brief says collapse is for candidates that give every external input the same old-side value; this collapses by observations, which is weaker and is what the outside review's rationale asks for (no question between mappings with no observable difference).

Verified inline: 5 new tests in lib/tests/alignment.rs, run by the own checker on one-line methods (the offset defect refuted with no mapping hiding it; a type-only question settled by the one mapping that holds; a sum's two orders collapsed; a changed result with two proved relations asked; the outcome rules on made-up attempts), 22 pass; 4 new scorer tests in examples/tools/test_alignment.py, 23 OK; the static scores on 121-139 unchanged (re-recorded under the new tool hash); the full cargo suite passes; the integration contract 2 passed, 22 unsupported, 0 failed.

Verification pending: job 20261107-053806-alignment-a3-second-half-every-proposal (verification/jobs/, quick, priority 10) runs alignment.py score --step proofs over examples 121-139 and should find every verified example's hand-written mapping proved, no mapping proved for any violation, and nothing wrong and accepted.

The first half of A3 is committed: `jvmcontract align` now proposes, for each method pair it matches, how the old version's arguments are built from the new inputs and how the two results compare. It doesn't prove anything yet.

**How it decides**
- **Inputs fixed by the contract:** if the preservation contract fixes an input, it maps to itself and nothing else. The contract comes from the new `--contract` option, or for a standalone method from the parameters both versions share by name and type.
- **No arithmetic:** a proposal is only ever a name, a field path, an integer cast or a record built with its constructor. So the offset mapping `before.c = after.c + 1` can't be proposed; a test plants it, with and without a contract.
- **Changed inputs:** these get ranked candidates, such as `batchStart` → `this.start`, or the old receiver rebuilt as `new Backoff(this.baseMillis, this.capMillis)`. A tie, or a match on type alone, becomes a question, and a new input that nothing uses is left free.
- **Results:** they come from a small catalogue: equal, widened, wrapped or unwrapped from a one-field record, or compared on the old record's fields. A result whose meaning changed (a boolean that became a number) is always a question with six candidates. Every observation the old version is held to stays counted.
- **Hints file:** proposals are written there as proposed and unchecked, with the reasons for each.

I've finished and committed A4's narrow case: `align::propose` now proposes the joint example's internal relation, and both of the stream's integration checks pass on this branch.

**What it does.** For a class whose fields changed between builds, the new `lib/src/alignment/fields.rs` gives each old field as a path into the new object:
- It reads which fields each version's constructor sets directly from a parameter.
- It pairs the old constructor with the new one the method matching (A2) picked, and maps the old constructor's parameters by the A3 rules: names, types, positions, record components, integral casts, never arithmetic.
- Putting the two together gives `old.q.cents == new.q.amount.cents` and `old.q.quantity == new.q.quantity`.
- The input `q` stays fixed to itself, as the contract says; only its internal fields are related.
- A field set any other way (computed, wrapped in a new object, or shifted like `this.cents = cents + 1`) is reported as unsupported, and nothing partial is proposed.

**Verification.**
- **Integration contract:** `alignment propose after` and `alignment propose offset` pass (2 passed, 22 unsupported, 0 failed). `after` gets exactly the golden correspondence; `offset` gets the same equations and no shifted input.
- **Tests:** three new tests in `lib/tests/alignment.rs` cover the joint example, a renamed field with a new field left free, and constructors that wrap or shift the value. All 17 alignment tests and the whole cargo suite pass.

Committed as `ptlmkomn` (634564ee): "Alignment A4: nested shapes, a field whose own class changed shape related through that class".

**What it does now:**
- **Nested fields are related.** An old field set from a constructor parameter whose own class changed shape is related through that class's correspondence. For example, a `Q` holding an `L` whose `cents` became `amount.cents` gives `old.q.line.cents == new.q.line.amount.cents`.
  - A candidate is only as sure as the less sure of its two steps, so a question inside stays a question.
  - A new field of the inner class is left free at its path (`line.tag`).
  - If the inner class can't be related, the outer field is reported as unsupported, with the inner reason named.
- **What it doesn't follow:** anything deeper than three levels, or a class that holds its own class (`N next`). Relating those needs a relation over a chain of objects, not field paths, so it is named and nothing is proposed.
- **Fixed on the way:** the check for whether a class changed only looked at the class's own fields, so a `Q` whose `L` changed counted as unchanged. It now looks all the way down. As a result:
  - such an input is no longer treated as fixed just because both signatures take it;
  - such a result is no longer called "equal"; it is left for a person to decide until results get their own equations, the next item.

**Verification:**
- One new test with three cases; all 26 alignment tests pass, and so does the whole cargo suite.
